subject: science

entries: Mitochondria: folded cristae, huge surface area: the inner membrane folds into cristae, packing a huge surface area for the enzymes that make ATP.
slots.label: Mitochondria
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: plants only respire at night: aerobic respiration runs around the clock, glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy, even while photosynthesis dominates by day.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: ATP hydrolysis releases energy; respiration rebuilds ATP: hydrolysis splits ATP to ADP and releases energy, and respiration in the mitochondrion rebuilds ATP from ADP.
slots.label: ATP hydrolysis releases energy; respiration rebuilds ATP
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Anaerobic: yeast → ethanol + CO₂; muscle → lactic acid: without enough oxygen glucose is only partly broken down, yielding far less ATP either way.
slots.label: Anaerobic
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Photolysis splits water; the Calvin cycle fixes CO₂: light splits water in the thylakoids and releases oxygen, then the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into glucose in the stroma.
slots.label: Photolysis splits water; the Calvin cycle fixes CO₂
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Photosynthesis is limited by the factor in shortest supply: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration or temperature - whichever is shortest caps the rate.
slots.label: Photosynthesis is limited by the factor in shortest supply
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The organelle where aerobic respiration rebuilds ATP, with a folded inner membrane.
slots.label: Mitochondrion
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane, giving a huge surface area for respiratory enzymes.
slots.label: Cristae
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Adenosine triphosphate, the energy currency of the cell; its hydrolysis releases usable energy.
slots.label: ATP
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Adenosine diphosphate, the spent form left after ATP hydrolysis, rebuilt into ATP by respiration.
slots.label: ADP
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The complete breakdown of glucose using oxygen, to carbon dioxide and water, yielding about 32 ATP per glucose.
slots.label: Aerobic respiration
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The partial breakdown of glucose without oxygen: yeast makes ethanol and carbon dioxide, muscle makes lactic acid, with far less ATP.
slots.label: Anaerobic respiration
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The splitting of water by light energy in the thylakoids, releasing oxygen.
slots.label: Photolysis
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The cycle in the stroma that fixes carbon dioxide and builds it up into glucose.
slots.label: Calvin cycle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
